items.body: Matching shardspaces can still be invalid. Setting both `p.Shardspace` and the configured specification to `wkeys.Shardspace(99)` passes validation and starts the factory. Every subsequent Walker acquisition fails because `NewReliableShardClientWithContext` calls `ShardKey.Validate`, which rejects that value. The existing negative test changes only one side, so it misses this case.
items.suggestion: Validate the shardspace enum before constructing resources; test matching invalid shardspaces.
items.title: Matching shardspaces can still be invalid

items.body: The positive-generation check accepts `2147483648` on both target platforms. `NewHistoryBranchHelper` converts that value to `int32`, producing a negative generation. HEWAL read/write decisions then disable HEWAL and select legacy persistence, which this factory explicitly rejects. Construction succeeds with a configuration that cannot persist workflow history.
items.suggestion: Require the generation to fit a positive `int32`; add an overflow boundary test.
items.title: The positive-generation check accepts `2147483648` on both target platforms

items.body: Successful owned-registry initialization has no cleanup guard covering subsequent construction. For example, otherwise valid parameters with `Config.ElementLockModeConfig = nil` pass validation, start the owned registry, then panic in `NewHistoryAppController`. The registry’s refresh goroutine and SQL metadata handle remain open. The existing panic-cleanup test covers only failures inside registry initialization.
items.suggestion: Defer owned-resource cleanup until ownership transfers to the returned factory, preserving unexpected panics. Add a regression test for a failure after registry startup.
items.title: Successful owned-registry initialization has no cleanup guard covering subsequent construction

## Issue 1
- **Severity**: P2
- **Title**: Matching shardspaces can still be invalid
- **Confidence**: 100
- **Classification**: introduced
- **Problem**: Matching shardspaces can still be invalid. Setting both `p.Shardspace` and the configured specification to `wkeys.Shardspace(99)` passes validation and starts the factory. Every subsequent Walker acquisition fails because `NewReliableShardClientWithContext` calls `ShardKey.Validate`, which rejects that value. The existing negative test changes only one side, so it misses this case.
- **Suggestion**: Validate the shardspace enum before constructing resources; test matching invalid shardspaces.

## Issue 2
- **Severity**: P2
- **Title**: The positive-generation check accepts `2147483648` on both target platforms
- **Confidence**: 100
- **Classification**: introduced
- **Problem**: The positive-generation check accepts `2147483648` on both target platforms. `NewHistoryBranchHelper` converts that value to `int32`, producing a negative generation. HEWAL read/write decisions then disable HEWAL and select legacy persistence, which this factory explicitly rejects. Construction succeeds with a configuration that cannot persist workflow history.
- **Suggestion**: Require the generation to fit a positive `int32`; add an overflow boundary test.
- **File:Line**: cds/export/cds/injected_factory.go:151
- **R-IDs**: R1, R11

## Issue 3
- **Severity**: P2
- **Title**: Successful owned-registry initialization has no cleanup guard covering subsequent construction
- **Confidence**: 100
- **Classification**: introduced
- **Problem**: Successful owned-registry initialization has no cleanup guard covering subsequent construction. For example, otherwise valid parameters with `Config.ElementLockModeConfig = nil` pass validation, start the owned registry, then panic in `NewHistoryAppController`. The registry’s refresh goroutine and SQL metadata handle remain open. The existing panic-cleanup test covers only failures inside registry initialization.
- **Suggestion**: Defer owned-resource cleanup until ownership transfers to the returned factory, preserving unexpected panics. Add a regression test for a failure after registry startup.
- **File:Line**: cds/export/cds/injected_factory.go:89
- **R-IDs**: R11, R6
